The character was created by artist Bob Kane and writer Bill Finger, and first appeared in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. Batman is the alter ego of Bruce Wayne, a wealthy and philanthropic playboy who dons a bat-themed costume to fight crime in Gotham City. Originally, Batman's crime-fighting origins focused on a vow of vengeance against the mobster who murdered his parents, Thomas and Martha Wayne.

He is often depicted as a solitary vigilante who operates in the shadows, using fear and intimidation to fight crime.

Batman has been adapted into various forms of media, including television series, movies, video games, and merchandise. He is one of the most popular and recognizable superheroes in the world.

Batman is a fictional character, a superhero who first appeared in Detective Comics #27 in 1939. He does not possess superhuman abilities but relies on his combat training, detective skills, martial arts, and an extensive array of gadgets to combat crime and take down criminals. He is often accompanied by his loyal butler, Alfred Pennyworth, and his often-mentored teenage sidekick, Robin.
